Mia (SE): quick sync — ACME trial asking for a 3-week eval. Need rough capacity and cost to confirm scope.
Mia (SE): short profile below, can folks sanity-check?
Mia (SE): ```
Traffic profile:
- 1k DAU, peak 25 concurrent sessions
- Avg user: 1 prompt (1.2k tokens) + model reply (0.8k tokens) per interaction
- Peak qps ~40 for ~2 minute bursts, baseline 3-5 qps
- Context window: 4k tokens (they want retrieval context included)
- Success criteria: 90% of eval prompts meet quality threshold; 95th p50 latency < 500ms; cost <= $12k/month for POC window
```
Owen (Infra): ok thanks. That profile is helpful. Quick take: with 4k context and those token sizes we need GPUs with 80GB-ish memory (A100/H100).
Owen (Infra): for latency target ~<500ms 95p, I’d size to 2x H100 80GB dedicated for steady-state, with autoscale to 4x for bursts.
Owen (Infra): if customer will accept fp16 + int8 quant, we can probably drop to 2x A100 80GB but expect quality differences.
Leah (PM): can you also split success criteria into functional and perf? we need an eval set (200 prompts) + baseline model outputs to compare.
Leah (PM): functional = 90% pass on correctness/formatting. Perf = 95p latency and error rate <0.5%.
Sanju (AE): budget note — ACME approved up to $10k for the trial (one-time credits). Can we fit within that?
Owen (Infra): with hosted (pay-as-you-go) estimate: rough exec cost for the token volumes during a 3-week ramp ~ $3k–$6k depending on batching/quant. Dedicated reserved 2x H100 monthly run ~ $7k–$9k (pro-rated for POC). Storage/ingest negligible.
Mia (SE): so it sounds doable within $10k one-time if we run hosted for the ramp and only provision dedicated if they want predictable throughput.
Nina (Sec): heads-up — ACME needs SSO + data residency in us-east-1 and an export control clause. I’ll push the SAQ and the security questionnaire today.
Mia (SE): action items: 1) Leah to provide 200 canonical prompts + success rubric. 2) Owen to give a short runbook for the 2x H100 config and expected 95p numbers. 3) Nina to share sec Q responses. 4) Sanju to confirm customer can accept hosted POC credits.
Leah (PM): I’ll drop the prompts into the shared drive by EOD. Also tagging a note: include 30 adversarial prompts for regression checks.
Owen (Infra): runbook snippet for sizing (quick):
```
- Base: 2x H100 80GB (dedicated), model: LLM-4k-context fp16
- Burst policy: auto-scale +2 nodes for sustained >30 qps for 2min
- Batching: target latency-friendly batch window 20-30ms, aggregate ~64 tokens/batch
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (expect 10-20% token savings)
- Quantization: test int8 in eval only (quality-run)
Estimated perf: 95p latency ≈ 300-450ms depending on prompt length
Estimated cost (pro-rated 3 weeks): dedicated ~$5k–$7k, hosted ~$3k–$6k
```
Sanju (AE): perfect, that pro-rated estimate maps to their $10k credit if we lean hosted for the ramp. Good to call out potential overrun if they hit sustained bursts.
Mia (SE): any red flags on model compatibility or rollout?
Owen (Infra): only risk is very long retrieval contexts pushing memory. If context regularly >3.7k tokens we may need the 4x config. Recommend instrumenting an early metric to track context-length distribution during the first 48h.
Nina (Sec): also need to confirm customer PII handling in prompts. Ask them to mark sensitive fields so we can apply redaction/CWE rules in ingest.
Leah (PM): timeline proposal: Week0 = config + data ingest + sec signoff; Week1 = run A vs B (fp16 vs quant) on eval set; Week2 = staged ramp with 1% traffic -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days; Week3 = soak + final metrics and handoff.
Mia (SE): I'll communicate timeline + budget to ACME and ask for the 200 prompts and sample logs.
deploy-bot: New runbook created: https://console.redwood/runbooks/ACME-trial-1934567890
Sanju (AE): I'll confirm with the buyer that hosted credits are acceptable and push for SSO details.
Mia (SE): thanks everyone — check-ins Thurs AM after Leah uploads prompts. :thumbsup:
